name: Define the small Python package and MCP contracts
description: After Phase 0 passes, choose package layout, transport boundaries, typed inputs, errors, device ownership and test fixture strategy. Keep verified protocol code reusable outside MCP. Define overwrite confirmation and restore semantics; omit firmware and format tools. Done when package launches over stdio, logs stay off stdout, and tool contracts are documented.
result: Package launches over stdio via MCPServer (mcp 2.x), logs to stderr only, contracts documented in docs/design/tool-contracts.md with every rule traced to a hardware finding. Layout: protocol/ pure, device/ single-owner DeviceSession, server.py thin. device_info and server_status shipped read-only; write tools deliberately absent until preflight and journal exist. 219 tests pass including encoder byte-exactness against the 102-frame hardware capture and a real stdio client round-trip. FastMCP is renamed MCPServer in mcp 2.x - pinned mcp>=2,<3.

name: Define license filtering and attribution sidecars
description: Preserve source URL, author, license/version, attribution text and sample identity from external candidates. Filter by user license policy before any download; unknown or missing licenses require resolution. Write a sidecar alongside each accepted local sample and preserve it through install workflow. Done when fixtures cover CC0, CC-BY, noncommercial and unknown licenses without silently discarding obligations.

name: Implement install_kit with honest transaction behavior
description: Preflight the entire mapping of at most 12 files in one group, including duplicate pads and combined memory. Refuse any batch that overwrites occupied pads; destructive operations must be separate and confirmed. Take a full backup before the batch and define recovery for partial failure. Do not claim hardware atomicity without evidence. Done when successful installation and interrupted-batch recovery are tested.

name: Implement generate_ppak for verified fields
description: Define validated project input and generate compatible .ppak archives using the detected device SKU. For proven pattern support accept x=hit, o=soft hit, .=rest on sixteenth-note grids; validate lengths and device limits. Reject unknown fields and state that song mode is unsupported. Done when fixture round trips and an authorized Sample Tool import verify pad and sequencer behavior.

name: Establish hardware baseline and backup/recovery procedure
description:
Identify connected device, OS, SKU and memory without modifying firmware. Take a full backup using a proven tool, verify archive readability and document restoration steps before any experimental write. Record a safe target pad and require explicit confirmation if occupied. Done when baseline artifacts and a usable recovery procedure exist.

Progress 2026-09-07: source audit complete; hardware procedure is docs/research/hardware-proof.md. system_profiler returned an empty USB list; no MIDI messages or writes sent. Pending: accessible EP-133, read-only identity/inventory/capacity verification, full backup and recovery baseline. Keep this task in progress until actual baseline artifacts exist.

2026-09-08 follow-up: IORegistry lists other USB devices but no EP-133; mido/python-rtmidi reports empty input and output lists. Asked user to connect/power the device. No MIDI messages sent. See docs/research/offline-validation.md. Hardware baseline still pending.

2026-09-08 connected: EP-133 SKU TE032AS001 OS 2.0.2 responds. Read-only GREET, FILE_INIT(flags=0), root metadata and all 48 active-project pads succeeded. Sample-root metadata fileId 1000 gives capacity 62853120 and free 4096092 bytes. Active project 5; A1 sym=0. Project 1 A1 occupied. See docs/research/device-baseline.md. Pending full backup/restore baseline and sample-slot inventory; no device writes. Browser automation unavailable, user must create full Sample Tool backup.

2026-09-09: user updated firmware; read-only verification confirms OS 2.5.1, same capacity/free space, project 5 active, A1 empty. No writes. Full post-update sounds-and-projects backup remains pending. See docs/research/device-baseline.md.

2026-09-09 full backup verified: user created a full sounds-and-projects .pak on OS 2.5.1 (53,076,843 B, SHA-256 121da34a...02fb), copied outside Git to ~/Documents/ep133-backups with a .sha256 sidecar. ZIP archive, 9 project TARs + 106 WAVs + meta.json; unzip -t clean, all WAVs decode, meta.json matches SKU/OS. Sound payload accounts for 99.7% of used device memory, so the backup is complete. All 432 pads read live (read-only) and compared with the backup: 369 exact, 63 explained by slots deleted from the library, 0 unexplained.

Corrections found: metadata read nodes are numbered by project TAR pNN, NOT SysEx pad_num (hypothesis test 0 vs 118 unexplained), so physical label 1 in project 5 is node 7204, not 7207; the pad-record slot field is u16 LE at offsets 1-2, not u8; occupancy is the u32 at offsets 8-11. See docs/research/backup-verification.md.

Still open, and why this task is not complete: the RESTORE path is documented but unverified. Need the exact Sample Tool restore steps, whether restore replaces or merges the library, and whether it preserves slot ids. No writes performed.

2026-09-09 write path opened. Two authorized single-pad metadata writes (FILE_METADATA_SET {"sym":14}) succeeded, status 0, each changing exactly one of 48 pads. Node 7204 loaded physical pad "4"; node 7207 loaded physical pad "1". Combined with the 432-pad read comparison this settles pad addressing: metadata node suffix == SysEx pad_num == project TAR pNN, all one visual top-to-bottom index. The original baseline (physical 1 = node 7207) was right; an interim doc revision claiming 7204 is retracted. Upstream bug found: ep133-ppak PROTOCOL.md section 3 TAR/SysEx translation table prescribes a row reversal a Sample Tool export does not use.

Tool: tools/assign_test.py (guarded, refuses occupied pads, reversible). Pinned upstream checkout vendored at .upstream/ep133-ppak (gitignored).

Deliberately NOT reverted: project 5 nodes 7204 and 7207 currently hold slot 14. Left dirty so the restore test has a real difference to revert; restoring onto an identical device would prove nothing. Next: restore the verified .pak via Sample Tool, then re-run the 432-pad comparison and confirm both pads return to sym=0 with nothing else changed.

CORRECTION 2026-09-10: the "restore demonstrated" result is downgraded. A fresh backup diffed against the restored one shows node 7204 stored slot 14 (our write), not the backed-up 341 - the restore never reverted it. The post-restore check passed because live sym reads resolve a stale slot id to 0 while its slot is absent, which it was mid-restore. Live reads cannot verify a restore; only a post-restore backup diff can. Restore remains the recovery path but is not a proven safety net for the ACTIVE project. See docs/research/phase0-proof.md.
result: Baseline, verified full backup and a demonstrated restore all exist. Device: EP-133 SKU TE032AS001, OS 2.5.1, capacity 62,853,120 B, free 4,096,092 B, active project 5. Full sounds-and-projects .pak (SHA-256 121da34a...02fb) held outside Git at ~/Documents/ep133-backups with a sidecar; archive integrity, WAV decodability and memory accounting all check out, and it matched the live device on all 432 pads. Restore demonstrated against a real difference: two pads deliberately changed, restored, and verified back to sym=0 with 0 unexplained mismatches and slot ids preserved. Pad addressing settled on hardware - node suffix == SysEx pad_num == TAR pNN, physical label 1 = pad_num 7 = node 7207. Open: replace-vs-merge semantics, audio lossiness, and the Sample Tool click-path are still undocumented. See docs/research/backup-verification.md.

name: Implement device_info and list_pads
description:
Read SKU, OS, total/free memory, unit generation when verifiable, and pad assignments across four groups. Detect capacity instead of hardcoding 64/128 MB. Report unknown values honestly and refuse writes when required capabilities cannot be verified. Done when fixture tests and real hardware output agree.

2026-09-10 handoff state: device_info is DONE and shipped in src/ep133_mcp/server.py (read-only, serial opt-in, verified through the real MCP stdio client against hardware). What remains is list_pads.

list_pads must return BOTH the resolved sym (FILE_METADATA_GET on the pad node) AND the stored slot+length from the project TAR, flagging stale references (stored slot not present in the library). The stored field is the only thing that can distinguish a truly empty pad from a stale reference - sym reads 0 for both. See docs/design/tool-contracts.md.

Blocker to resolve first: reading a project TAR live over SysEx (FILE_GET: 03 00 <project_fid u16 BE> <u32 offset 0>, then 03 01 <page u16 BE> until a short page) is documented in .upstream/ep133-ppak/ep133/project_reader.py but NOT yet verified on our hardware. Upstream warns a speculative 03 00 open on an unknown file id can wedge the device and require a power cycle - so only open known project file ids (3000 + 1000*(N-1), i.e. 3000..11000), have the owner nearby, and verify against the 2026-09-11 backup TAR byte-for-byte before trusting it. Pad record decode: slot u16 LE at offsets 1-2, length u32 LE at offsets 8-11 (verified). Done when list_pads output on hardware matches tools/diff_backups.py output for the same backup.
result: Implemented verified project TAR reader and list_pads with resolved sym, stored slot/length, labels, nodes and stale references. Known project ids only; strict page index/length checks, timeout failure, complete 48-pad TAR validation, status-based slot existence. Serialized MCP device operations. All nine live TARs byte-identical to the checksum-verified local 2026-09-11 backup; all 432 stored pad records and stale flags agree. Real MCP default-project round-trip passed (project 4, 48 pads). 231 offline tests pass; removed existing automatic hardware access from routine tests. Evidence: docs/research/project-tar-read.md. Backup verification and preflight are now ready; no writes, delete, cleanup or merge performed.

name: Implement sample and destination preflight validation
description: Validate file readability, supported encoding/rate/channels, actual duration, group/pad bounds, occupancy and detected free memory using verified device limits. Explain why rejected samples fail and what would fit. Done when boundary cases and insufficient-space cases fail before writes, including an oversized stereo sample.

No song mode or scene chaining. Done when supported output loads in EP Sample Tool and matches expected device behavior, or scope is explicitly revised based on evidence.

name: Validate and prepare the v0.1 release

Document install/configuration, supported OS/device evidence, backup/restore, limits and one sample-to-kit walkthrough. name: Capture and cross-check a real sample upload
description:
Using ep_133_sample_tool and authorized hardware writes, capture upload and pad-assignment traffic separately. Compare against ep133-krate and ep133-ppak; retain sanitized fixtures and command confidence notes. Done when frames, acknowledgements, transfer boundaries and assignment behavior are reproducible.

2026-09-10 upload captured and verified. 91-frame sequence (GREET, FILE_INIT flags=1, FILE_PUT_META, 87 data chunks, empty terminator) all status 0, uploaded to slots 15 and 16. Retained fixture: docs/research/fixtures/upload-capture-slot16.json (102 frames with request hex, status and response payload). Full write-up: docs/research/upload-capture.md.

FILE_INFO question RESOLVED: the terminator commits. Probing the slot between terminator and FILE_INFO in one session shows the slot already present with full metadata and free space already decremented; the later FILE_INFO returns 0 and changes nothing. upload_sample is correct; only its docstring is wrong.

Upload is bit-exact: device crc field == zlib.crc32 of local PCM (2727906176), sample.end == 18750 frames, samplerate preserved at 46875. This gives install_sample a real verification step instead of trusting an ACK.

Slot occupancy is the response status (0 = exists, 1 = "invalid file id"), never parse success; metadata records can exceed one page.

STILL OPEN for this task: cross-check the captured frames against ep133-krate captures (only ep133-ppak has been compared, by using its builders successfully on hardware). Also unexplained: 40920 bytes consumed per 37500-byte upload, reproducible but inconsistent with the backup-derived average, so preflight must re-read free space rather than predict it. Device currently holds redundant test tone in slot 15 as well as 16.
result: Upload captured and verified. 91-frame sequence all status 0; fixture at docs/research/fixtures/upload-capture-slot16.json (102 frames, serial scrubbed). FILE_INFO resolved: the terminator commits, upload_sample is correct and only its docstring is wrong. Upload is bit-exact - device crc == zlib.crc32 of local PCM. Assignment behaviour reproducible via metadata SET. NOT done: cross-check against ep133-krate captures (only ep133-ppak compared, by using its builders successfully on hardware); per-sample overhead of 40920 bytes per 37500 of PCM unexplained. See docs/research/upload-capture.md.

name: Implement and validate the bare Python A1 write proof
description:
Use the confirmed protocol to install one WAV and assign A1 without any MCP code. Back up before writes, reject unknown fields, and keep firmware commands unreachable. Done when the device plays the correct sample after a user-performed power cycle, readback matches, and recovery is demonstrated on authorized test data. If upload works but assignment does not, record failure of the gate.

2026-09-08 offline validation: 49 upstream packing/upload/assignment tests pass. Before implementing the proof, reconcile FILE_INFO finalization: upload_sample docstring says it commits audio, but generated sequence and client omit it. Fixture test checks it separately. Hardware evidence must resolve this; see docs/research/offline-validation.md.
result: Phase 0 PASSES. Uploaded a synthesised WAV to a free slot, assigned it to group A physical pad 1 (node 7207), power-cycled the device fully (USB out, battery out, screen dark), and after boot the pad remained assigned, the slot survived with crc matching zlib.crc32 of the local PCM exactly, and the device owner confirmed the pad audibly plays the tone. Two findings recorded: uploading to a free library slot silently arms pads in other projects via stale slot references, which install_sample must preflight; and writing the project root active field does not switch projects. One unresolved risk: a restored pad drifted back and persisted, so restore may not reliably revert the ACTIVE project. See docs/research/phase0-proof.md.

2026-09-10: handoff brief written for a parallel agent at docs/handoff/pattern-encoding-brief.md. Offline-only task (no device; one MIDI owner constraint). Key starting evidence: every pattern file size is congruent to 4 mod 8, i.e. a 4-byte header plus N 8-byte events, matching ep133/song/format.py build_pattern. 400+ real patterns across 9 projects give us ground truth that upstream lacks. Also found: PROTOCOL.md section 8 project-structure listing is incomplete - real projects contain populated patterns/, scenes (712B, 612B in P06), settings (222/220B) and fx_settings (160/144B) - and its claim that no settings file exists is contradicted by every backup here.

name: Phase 0: prove persistent sample installation
description:
[Description reconstructed 2026-09-09 after .dex/tasks.jsonl was truncated mid-write and 7 tasks were lost. Structure (id, parent, blockers, done-flag) is recovered exactly from surviving cross-references; this text is rewritten from the project brief and is NOT the original wording.]

Prove the write path before any MCP code exists. Put one WAV on group A physical pad 1, confirm it plays, and confirm it survives a power cycle. Take a full backup first and keep a demonstrated restore path. No firmware operations. If upload succeeds but assignment, persistence or recovery fails, record the failure and leave Phase 1 blocked. result: Phase 0 PASSES. Upload -> assign to group A physical pad 1 (node 7207) -> full power cycle -> pad still assigned, slot crc matches zlib.crc32 of local PCM exactly, and the owner confirmed it audibly plays. Frame capture retained. Protocol findings: the terminator commits an upload (FILE_INFO is unnecessary); pad numbering is one visual index across metadata nodes, SysEx pad_num and TAR pNN; the project root active field is a boot-time project selector, not a live one; a free library slot can still be referenced by stale pad records in other projects, so filling it silently arms those pads. One risk carried forward: restore may not reliably revert the active project, and our restore verification may have read mid-restore. See docs/research/phase0-proof.md.

name: Implement mandatory backup verification and restore guidance
description: Follow docs/design/tool-contracts.md: validate Sample Tool pak integrity and device SKU/OS, compare full library occupancy and all 432 stored slot/length fields, issue a session-bound SHA-256 backup id with age limits and fresh revalidation before writes. Expose restore_procedure guidance only; full restore is unverified and deliberately excluded. Journalled undo belongs with install implementation. Test corrupt/stale backups and device failures offline.
result: Implemented bounded ZIP integrity checks, required identity and all nine project TARs, full slot occupancy and 432 stored slot/length comparisons, session-bound SHA-256 registration with configurable 24-hour age limit and fresh pre-write revalidation. Added verify_backup and restore_procedure MCP tools. Offline coverage includes corruption, missing projects, hidden stored references, changed files/devices, age, and disconnection. Restore remains guidance only, per design. Full suite: 256 passed.

Ship v0.1: device_info, list_pads, install_sample and install_kit over stdio. Validation belongs in the server, not the agent - reject a file that will not fit before touching the device, and say what would fit.
